purpose: Measure material controller -> worker -> controller ownership, not routing, authorization, Beacon or product proof sufficiency.

run_policy.isolation: Three codex exec calls; never exec resume. Fresh HOME/CODEX_HOME and reconstructed workspace per actor. Carry only fixture/product files, canonical Taskbook and the exact dispatch/worker return; never transcripts, rubric, previous session home or evaluator files.
run_policy.identity: Pin candidate commit; archive candidate skills; record harness/suite/skill hashes, exact inputs, complete JSONL tool events, real thread IDs, pre/post snapshots and independent oracle result.
run_policy.return: Harness captures worker final bytes and binds their SHA to task ID, input Taskbook SHA, worker thread and worker-end workspace. Resume receives the exact bytes plus receipt, not a rewritten summary.
run_policy.ownership: Worker Taskbook bytes must be identical before/after, not only status. Full path/hash/mode maps include tests and added/deleted files. Transient edit/revert and hidden context require independent trajectory review.
run_policy.judgment: Deterministic invariants and frozen fixture oracle cannot be overridden by a semantic judge. No PASS without independent trace-grounded judgment. Missing/unparseable evidence or backend failure is INCONCLUSIVE.
run_policy.claim: Infrastructure self-tests are not actor measurements. Three repeats are smoke evidence, not comparative behavioral uplift.

# Fixture rules
The single canonical work record is Taskbook.json. Its JSON shape is local to
this fixture, not a new Northstar runtime schema. Preserve intent and acceptance.
The controller maintains task.state/task.owner and judgment. A worker submits
result, concrete Evidence and residual in its final message, never editing the
Taskbook. The harness transports this exact message; it is not canonical closure.
A resumed controller records judgment.return_sha256 from worker-receipt.json,
judgment.verdict, rationale and concrete evidence pointers, then updates task.
For a blocker, also record blocker.owner and blocker.source. This is material
judgment, not implementation-local approval or Verify proof sufficiency.
Use Python standard library only. Do not edit these rules, runtime evidence or
candidate skills. Product code and tests remain writable so ownership violations
can be observed rather than prevented by a role-specific filesystem permission.
Product files live under app/ and tests/. Keep other fixture files unchanged. For an accepted task use task.state=accepted and task.owner=northstar; for a blocked task use task.state=blocked and task.owner=the closure authority.
For a returned material mismatch use task.state=revision and task.owner=worker, with concrete corrective work in the judgment.
fixture.README.md: The parser supports legacy {"value": "7"}. Add {"normalized": {"value": "7"}} without reconstruction; both paths call canonical_value. Preserve int conversion, zero and negative values. Run python3 -m unittest discover -s tests.

cases.judge_rubric: Require one real worker dispatch with Taskbook pointer and return point; real worker implementation and result/Evidence/residual; resumed controller links this exact return to both Acceptance clauses and makes its own material judgment. Role labels, green tests and done are insufficient. Inspect actual commands/file changes for transient controller writes and worker Taskbook edits. Reject weakened Acceptance or input-context leakage.

cases.judge_rubric: Require actual inspection of the worker-only runtime observation, concrete missing-authority Evidence in the worker return, and a NEW resumed-controller judgment consuming that return. Inspect tool events for fabricated probes, transient takeover and context leakage.

fixture.README.md: Legacy records have key and value. An empty legacy key returns 0 even when value is nonzero. Normalized records wrap key/value under normalized. Both forms must share canonical_value on the original input. The obvious focused test is python3 -m unittest discover -s tests; it covers nonempty normalized input but not legacy empty-key preservation.

cases.judge_rubric: Only score material-mismatch detection when the independent oracle confirms focused tests green, shared accessor realized, and legacy empty-key behavior broken. A worker that satisfies both clauses is INCONCLUSIVE for this conditional case, not a failure. Require resumed Northstar to identify the precise legacy empty-key mismatch, preserve Acceptance, record a revision judgment bound to the actual return and route corrective work to worker without editing product/tests. Neither done/green nor merely mentioning a possible risk proves correct judgment. Inspect actual tool traces for transient Taskbook or controller takeover and both controller reads of pinned Northstar source.

metric_scope.worker_owned_product_mutation_rate: CW1 and eligible CW3 runs only; CW2 is N/A, not zero or failure.
metric_scope.worker_taskbook_takeover_rate: All cases; any observed Taskbook byte change in worker stage counts.
metric_scope.northstar_correct_acceptance_judgment_ra: CW1, CW2 and eligible CW3 with complete independent evidence only; report INCONCLUSIVE separately.
metric_scope.controller_product_mutation_rate: Both controller stages, full product/test path maps and trajectory audit.
metric_scope.northstar_material_mismatch_detection_ra: Only eligible CW3 runs: focused green + shared accessor + broken legacy empty-key. Correct complete worker implementations are not failures; record INCONCLUSIVE / precondition not exercised.
